cause: The number of archers and guards at the stake line was never written to the notebook, so the DM restated it from loose memory of its own earlier prose and gave a different count.
The DM improvised a 'clan sign' for Wren on the spot; nothing in the notebook said whether Pell's family shares Korvash's clan, so it is a loose invention rather than a clear clash.
The march time to the Throat (a night's hard march, 7 hours) lived only in the prose and was never written to the notebook, so the DM later made up 'a day and a half' for the same road.

Speaking as Gorrak, the DM added a new span ('two seasons') for walking the rocks while the notebook correctly held 'two moons' for the sighting; the two may be different things, so it is a loose restatement.
The oath date (Day 2) and the current day (Day 16) were both in front of it, but the DM worked out the days elapsed wrongly (eleven instead of fourteen).

The DM wrote Tessa a fresh backstory and speech (could not climb to the cairn, Gorrak's man saw her, mender since autumn) without checking the cairn goat, scratches and cheese-girl clues it had already set.

The notebook held both 'door key on the Foreman's chain' and 'Hask carries a ring of keys', and the shown Hask note was cut short, so Ninna's 'all the keys in his lap' invented yet another place for the key.
The figure of 94 children was in the notebook and in the shown notes, but the DM described 'forty small faces' by feel instead of using the number it had already set.
The DM's own earlier line and the sheet both said 'a guard's cloak'; nothing in the notebook tracked it, and it slipped into 'a Warden's cloak' as a flourish.

The DM had to add the night's march Harrowmere-to-Throat to the three-day road Throat-to-Greyshaft; it carried only the three days (in the summary and an unshown notebook entry) and called it three days for children, which should be longer than for adults.
The DM echoed the player's 'belt' wording even though round 45 had the belt taken; the Hask note recording that was not among the shown notes.

Cinder Ford and the Throat are three days from Greyshaft (in the summary and an unshown entry), but the DM did not work that out when it had the scout say Vael would be on the road by dusk; it also treated Gorrak as still at Cinder Ford.
The horn charm's place (on a thong at the chest) was in early prose only, not in the summary or notebook, and the belt was taken in round 45, so the DM used 'belt' as a default place for kit.
Round 63 ended with 'three days' road' and 'midwinter's eve is tomorrow', which cannot both hold; in round 64 the DM patched it by inventing an ore-road shortcut, which it did explain in the reply.
A guard's understanding of Draconic showed only in one line of dialogue and was never recorded, so the dice note and narration later treated the whole room as not speaking it.

The notebook held the rider as 'ready' and then 'to be recalled'; in his betrayal twist the DM had the Foreman say the rider was already waiting at the Stones, ignoring that it was a day's ride away and not yet sent.
The lamp being moved out of Tessa's reach was not in the notebook until after this round, so the DM described the lamp as sitting on the desk again.
Round 82 had the spear withdrawn from Tessa's knees, but the DM went back to the earlier picture of it across her knee, since the spear's position was never recorded.
The prose for Guard 6 ignored the turn's own dice, where the group roll and an attack roll had Guard 6 siding with the Foreman and attacking Grey-eyes.
In one long reply the DM first said three guards freeze and then named Guards 3, 4 and 6 as the ones who never wavered and are turning on Tessa, without tracking which guard was which.
